operations.description: Sends a response to a pending human-in-the-loop (HITL) request for the specified session. Resolving a request unblocks the agent and emits an `intervention.resolved` webhook event when `requestId` is provided.

session_id.description: The ID of the browser session

requestId.description: ID of the intervention request to respond to. If omitted, the most recent pending request for the session is used.

response.description: Response payload. For `text` input type, pass a string. For `confirm`, pass a boolean or confirmation string. For `fields`, pass an object keyed by field name.

operations.name: Resume agent
operations.description: Resumes the AI agent for the specified browser session.

session_id.description: The ID of the browser session

operations.name: Pause session recording
operations.description: Pauses the video recording for the specified browser session.

session_id.description: The ID of the browser session for which to pause recording.

operations.name: Resume session recording
operations.description: Resumes the video recording for the specified browser session.

session_id.description: The ID of the browser session for which to resume recording.

operations.name: Create session tokens
operations.description: Mint URLs for a running session that can be handed to end users without exposing the session id. Each scope gets its own token, carried as `?token=` in the URL: - `live_view_read_only`: watch the browser only. - `live_view`: watch and interact with the browser. - `cdp`: full CDP control. Every call mints new tokens. A token stops working when the session ends or when it is revoked. On a session cr

session_id.description: The ID of the running session.

scopes.description: Token scopes to mint. Omit or pass an empty list to mint every scope the session can serve: all three, only `cdp` on a headless session, and no `live_view` on a `live_view.one_time_url` session.

operations.name: Create task (legacy)
operations.description: Creates a new task or updates an existing task with the same name. Tasks are reusable code snippets that can be executed in browser sessions. Tasks support versioning with draft and published versions. If you are using the new Task Builder, see the non-deprecated Tasks endpoints in this API reference.

name.description: Task name (letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores only)

operations.name: Run task (legacy)
operations.description: Executes a task in a browser session. The task can be run with a specific version or the latest version. Optionally, you can provide an existing session ID or let the system create a new one. If you are using the new Task Builder, see the non-deprecated Tasks endpoints in this API reference.

version.description: Version to run (draft, latest, or version number)

sessionId.description: Optional existing browser session ID to use for task execution

async.description: Whether to run the task asynchronously.

inputs.description: Environment variables for task execution (keys must start with ANCHOR_)

cleanupSessions.description: Whether to cleanup browser sessions after task execution. Defaults to true.

operations.name: Run task by name (legacy)
operations.description: Executes a task by its name, always using the latest version. This is a convenience endpoint for running tasks without needing to know the task ID. If you are using the new Task Builder, see the non-deprecated Tasks endpoints in this API reference.

taskName.description: The name of the task to run

sessionId.description: Optional existing browser session ID to use for task execution

async.description: Whether to run the task asynchronously

inputs.description: Environment variables for task execution (keys must start with ANCHOR_)

cleanupSessions.description: Whether to cleanup browser sessions after task execution. Defaults to true.

operations.name: Deploy task (legacy)
operations.description: Deploys a task by creating a new version with auto-incremented version number. This is the recommended way to publish task changes. If you are using the new Task Builder, see the non-deprecated Tasks endpoints in this API reference.

code.description: Base64 encoded task code (required for new versions)

operations.name: Create or update task draft (legacy)
operations.description: Creates or updates the draft version of a task. Draft versions are used for development and testing before publishing. If you are using the new Task Builder, see the non-deprecated Tasks endpoints in this API reference.

operations.name: Publish task version (legacy)
operations.description: Publishes a specific version of a task. This creates a new version if it doesn't exist, or updates an existing version's metadata. If you are using the new Task Builder, see the non-deprecated Tasks endpoints in this API reference.

taskVersion.description: The version to publish (cannot be draft)

code.description: Base64 encoded task code (required for new versions)

operations.name: Execute code snippet
operations.description: Run a TypeScript snippet in the sandbox against the browser session (query `sessionId` required).

sessionId.description: Browser session to run the snippet against.

code.description: TypeScript snippet (async function body) with injected page, browser, context, sessionId, anchorClient.

operations.name: Web unlocker
operations.description: Fetch the fully rendered HTML of any URL — including CAPTCHA- and bot-protected sites — with a single sessionless request. Each request runs in a stealth browser behind a residential proxy. JavaScript is fully rendered, cookie-consent dialogs are dismissed, and CAPTCHA or bot-detection challenges (Cloudflare, reCAPTCHA, FunCaptcha, DataDome, Kasada, Akamai, PerimeterX) are solved automatically — y

url.description: The fully-qualified URL to fetch, including the scheme (e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/company/openai`).

operations.name: Get page pdf
operations.description: Generates a PDF of the current page for a browser session and returns it as a binary PDF file.

sessionId.description: Optional browser session ID. If omitted, `url` in the request body is required.

url.description: The URL of the page to print to PDF.

displayHeaderFooter.description: Display header and footer. Defaults to false.

printBackground.description: Print background graphics. Defaults to false.

scale.description: Scale of the webpage rendering. Defaults to 1.

paperWidth.description: Paper width in inches. Defaults to 8.5.

paperHeight.description: Paper height in inches. Defaults to 11.

marginTop.description: Top margin in inches. Defaults to ~0.4.

marginBottom.description: Bottom margin in inches. Defaults to ~0.4.

marginLeft.description: Left margin in inches. Defaults to ~0.4.

marginRight.description: Right margin in inches. Defaults to ~0.4.

pageRanges.description: Page ranges to print, e.g. '1-5, 8, 11-13'. Defaults to all pages.

headerTemplate.description: HTML template for the print header.

footerTemplate.description: HTML template for the print footer.

preferCSSPageSize.description: Prefer page size as defined by CSS. Defaults to false.

operations.name: Perform web task
operations.description: Start from a URL and perform the given task.

sessionId.description: An optional browser session identifier to reference an existing running browser sessions. When passed, the tool will be executed on the provided browser session.

url.description: The URL of the webpage. If not provided, the tool will use the current page in the session.

prompt.description: The task to be autonomously completed.

agent.description: The AI agent to use for task completion. Defaults to browser-use.

provider.description: The AI provider to use for task completion.

model.description: The specific model to use for task completion. see our [models](/agentic-browser-control/ai-task-completion#available-models) page for more information.

detect_elements.description: Enable element detection for better interaction accuracy. Improves the agent's ability to identify and interact with UI elements.

human_intervention.description: Allow human intervention during task execution. When enabled, the agent can request human input for ambiguous situations.

max_steps.description: Maximum number of steps the agent can take to complete the task. Defaults to 200.

llm_timeout.description: Timeout in seconds for each LLM call made by the agent (browser-use agent only). Raise it when tasks with deep context (long histories, large pages) hit LLM call timeouts. When omitted, the agent uses its model-based defaults.

secret_values.description: Secret values to pass to the agent for secure credential handling. Keys and values are passed as environment variables to the agent.

highlight_elements.description: Whether to highlight elements during task execution for better visibility.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema defining the expected structure of the output data.

async.description: Whether to run the task asynchronously. If true, the task will be run asynchronously and the response will include a workflow ID.

operations.name: Screenshot webpage
operations.description: This endpoint captures a screenshot of the specified webpage using Chromium. Users can customize the viewport dimensions and capture options.

sessionId.description: An optional browser session identifier to reference an existing running browser sessions. When passed, the tool will be executed on the provided browser session.

url.description: The URL of the webpage to capture.

width.description: The width of the browser viewport in pixels.

height.description: The height of the browser viewport in pixels.

image_quality.description: Quality of the output image, on the range 1-100. 100 will not perform any compression.

wait.description: Duration in milliseconds to wait after page has loaded, mainly used for sites with JS animations.

scroll_all_content.description: If true, scrolls the page and captures all visible content.

capture_full_height.description: If true, captures the entire height of the page, ignoring the viewport height.

s3_target_address.description: Presigned S3 url target to upload the image to.

operations.name: Create volume
operations.description: Create a persistent volume for your team. The volume is usually `ready` immediately; if the response says `creating`, poll `GET /v1/volumes/{volume_id}` until it is. Each team can have up to 10 volumes.

name.description: Volume name, unique within your team. Letters, numbers, `_` and `-`, up to 64 characters.

operations.name: Create directory
operations.description: Create an empty folder in the volume. Folders are also created implicitly when a file is uploaded to a path inside them.

operations.name: Upload file
operations.description: Upload a file into the volume in one multipart request. For files larger than 10 MB use `POST /v1/volumes/{volume_id}/files/upload-url` instead.

path.description: Destination path relative to the volume root, e.g. `downloads/report.pdf`. Defaults to the uploaded file's name at the root.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at `path`. Defaults to `false`.

operations.name: Create upload url
operations.description: Get a pre-signed URL to upload a file of any size (up to 5 GB) directly to storage. `PUT` the file body to `signed_url` and send the returned `headers` unchanged.

path.description: Destination path relative to the volume root

content_type.description: MIME type of the file. Defaults to `application/octet-stream`.

operations.name: Generate a task
operations.description: Starts asynchronous generation of a new task from a natural-language prompt. Poll `GET /v2/tasks/{taskId}/generation-status` until the status is `ready`.

taskPrompt.description: Natural-language description of what the task should do, used for AI generation. Make it as detailed as possible with all the logic and steps needed to complete the task.

async.description: Whether to generate the task asynchronously

application_id.description: Optional application (connection) ID to associate with the task

identity_id.description: Optional identity ID to use during task generation

output_file_only.description: Whether task runs should return only the bundled session downloads file

human_intervention.description: Allow human intervention during task execution

browser_session_id.description: Existing finished browser session id to generate the workflow from

task_browser_default_configuration.description: Optional default browser/session configuration when running this task

operations.name: Run a task
operations.description: Triggers execution of a task by ID using the non-deprecated Tasks endpoints.

taskId.description: The ID of the task to run

input_params.description: Key-value pairs of input parameters for the task

identity_id.description: Optional identity ID to use for the task

session_id.description: Optional session ID to run the task in

cleanup_sessions.description: Whether to clean up sessions after execution (default: true)

identity_skip_validation.description: When `true` (default), skip profile validation for active identities and reuse the saved browser profile. Set to `false` to validate the profile and re-authenticate if it is no longer signed in. Pending identities still authenticate on first use.

sync.description: Wait for the task to complete before returning. Defaults to `false`.

operations.name: Update identity
operations.description: Updates an existing identity's name, metadata, or credentials.

identityId.description: The ID of the identity to update

operations.name: Put session tags
operations.description: Create or replace tags on a browser session. This overwrites any existing tags with the provided list. See [Session Tags](/advanced/session-tags).

session_id.description: The ID of the session to update tags for.

tags.description: Tags to set on the session. Replaces any existing tags.

operations.name: Update task metadata (legacy)
operations.description: Updates task metadata (name and description). This does not affect the task code or versions. If you are using the new Task Builder, see the non-deprecated Tasks endpoints in this API reference.

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

name.description: Task name (letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores only)

operations.name: Rotate webhook signing secret
operations.description: Mint a new HMAC-SHA256 signing secret. The previous secret remains valid for 24 hours so you can update your verification code at your own pace, then drop the old secret. The new secret is returned exactly once, in the `secret` field.

operations.name: Send test event
operations.description: Fire a synthetic event of the given type through the real signing + retry path. Useful during development for confirming your endpoint can verify the signature and is reachable from Anchor's egress IPs. The synthetic delivery counts toward your delivery log so you can see it in `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/events`.

event_type.description: Catalog of webhook event types Anchor can deliver. Adding a new event type is a coordinated change between session-manager (publisher), webhook-dispatcher (consumer), and the dashboard.

operations.name: Update webhook
operations.description: Partial update — pass only the fields you want to change. Setting `enabled: false` immediately stops events from fanning out to this webhook (existing in-flight deliveries finish their attempts).
